# A rename theirs made is dropped because its source is gone on our side. If the
# name it renamed TO is occupied by an unrelated user of ours, theirs' follow-up
# entries must not land on that user - they mean a different person.

sesam-repo

exec sesam tell --user alice --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add alice'

# OURS: alice is killed and an unrelated user that happens to be called bob joins.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sesam kill --user alice
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $CAROL_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: alice out, unrelated bob in'

# THEIRS: alice is renamed to bob and made an admin.
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sesam user rename alice bob
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group-add admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: alice -> bob, bob += admin'

exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs

# The rename is dropped, and the group change that rides on it is skipped rather
# than making OUR bob an admin.
stderr 'rename source alice gone on our side'
stderr 'references bob, whose rename/move was dropped on merge'
